candidates.title: Adaptive Parallelism for LLM Inference with Model Irrelevant Profiler
candidates.venue: International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design
candidates.abstract: The optimal parallel setup for an arbitrary target model deployment usually requires on-site hardware-software cooperative tuning, since it depends on not only model architecture and hyper-parameters, but also hardware configurations like GPU and networking, which brings extra human tuning efforts especially for private delivery cases. Inspired by GPU compute pattern analysis in tensor parallel sharding, an on-site tuning-free optimal parallel prediction method is proposed. In pre-profiling phase, a model irrelevant GPU profiler is introduced to evaluate GPU compute efficiency with common transformer block. And in deployment phase, the optimal parallel strategy is predicted according to pre-profiling results, available hardware resource and model hyper-parameters. It is further integrated into a parallel decision workflow for self-adaptive hybrid parallelism. In general, our proposal achieves 88% of best parallel adaption accuracy and less than 6% performance loss with failed cases, validated through 20+ different decode-only transformers based LLMs.
candidates.reason: モデル非依存のGPUプロファイラで共通Transformerブロックの計算効率を事前計測し、デプロイ先のハードウェアとモデル諸元から最適なテンソル並列構成を現地チューニングなしに予測する、LLM推論の並列度決定そのものを対象とした直接の貢献である。

candidates.title: Efficient Multi-Lora Deployment via Shared KV-Cache with Task-Adaptive Tokens
candidates.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
candidates.reason: SKV-TATは複数LoRAアダプタごとに独立していたKVキャッシュを、基底モデルのみで長い接頭辞を処理して共有キャッシュ化し、タスク適応トークンでタスク固有性を保つことで、資源制約下のマルチLoRA推論のメモリを直接削減する手法である。

candidates.title: SWAA: Sliding Window Attention Adaptation for Efficient Long-Context LLMs Without Pretraining
candidates.reason: 全注意で事前学習したLLMを再学習なしにスライディングウィンドウ注意へ適応させるSWAAは、学習・推論ミスマッチと遠方情報へのアクセス不能という二つの崩壊要因に対処し、二次計算量の長文脈推論を線形化する直接の注意効率化手法である。

candidates.title: A Fully Integrated Energy-Scalable Transformer Accelerator for Language Understanding on Edge Devices
candidates.venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Solid-State Circuits Society
candidates.abstract: Text and spoken language have become standard ways to interface with edge devices. Due to tight power and compute constraints, they require efficient natural language processing that can adapt the computation to the hardware conditions. This article presents a Transformer accelerator running a custom-trained SuperTransformer model from which SubTransformers of various sizes can be sampled enabling adaptive model configuration. The test chip contains a variable-depth adder tree to support different model dimensions, a word elimination unit to prune redundant tokens, and dedicated softmax and layer normalization units. It achieves up to <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$6.9\times $ </tex-math></inline-formula> scalability in network latency and energy between the largest and smallest SubTransformers, under the same operating conditions. Word elimination can reduce network energy by 16%, with a 14.5% drop in F1 score. At 0.68 V and 80 MHz, processing a 32-length input with our custom two-layer Transformer model for intent detection and slot filling takes 0.61 ms and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$1.6~\mu $ </tex-math></inline-formula>J.
candidates.reason: エッジデバイス向けにSuperTransformerから大きさの異なるSubTransformerを切り出せるエネルギー可変型Transformerアクセラレータを集積し、可変深さ加算木や冗長トークン除去ユニットで遅延とエネルギーを最大6.9倍スケールさせる、オンデバイス言語理解推論の直接のハードウェア貢献である。

candidates.title: Arlo: Serving Transformer-based Language Models with Dynamic Input Lengths
candidates.abstract: A prominent challenge in serving requests for NLP tasks is handling the varying length of input texts. Existing solutions, such as uniform zero-padding and compiler support, suffer from either computational inefficiency or suboptimal latency. To address these practical issues, we propose an approach called polymorphing. Polymorphing involves creating and utilizing multiple runtimes of the model, each statically compiled with a different input length, to serve requests accordingly. This fine-grained use of statically-compiled runtimes reduces the overheads of zero-padding while improving latency performance compared to dynamic compilation. To practically realize polymorphing, we have developed an inference scheduling system, Arlo, which leverages the observed input length distribution to periodically allocate compute resources across multiple runtimes by solving an integer linear program. Upon request arrival, Arlo uses a multi-level queue-based heuristic to dispatch requests to the most suitable runtime instances, efficiently adapting to the dynamics of request length and instance load. Extensive testbed evaluations and large-scale simulations using production traces demonstrate Arlo’s promising potential. It achieves 23.7%–98.1% mean latency reductions compared to existing schemes while significantly reducing tail latency.
candidates.reason: Arloは入力長ごとに静的コンパイルした複数ランタイムを用意し、入力長分布に応じて計算資源を周期的に配分する多形化によりゼロ埋めの無駄と動的コンパイルの遅延を避ける、Transformer言語モデルのサービングと推論スケジューリングの直接のシステムである。
